DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. 34 s.2021 Mar. 4, 2021 HON. EVANGELINE H. JUBAS Vice-Mayor Kauswagan, Lanao del Norte Dear Vice-Mayor Jubas: This has reference to your letter dated 17 December 2020 requesting this Department's opinion on various issues concerning the propriety of acts of the Sangguniang Bayan of Kauswagan, Province of Lanao del Norte. As can be culled from your letter and its attachments, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Kauswagan, Lanao del Norte, thru its SB Committee on Laws, Rules, Ethics and Good Government passed a Resolution Recommending to the Local Chief Executive Hon. Rommel C. Amado for the Suspension of Mr. Fortunato A. Densing, SB Secretary for not Submitting the Required Documents Requested by the HR Department. Ostensibly, prior to the passage of the aforesaid Resolution, the SB Committee on Laws, Rules, Ethics, Good Government and Public Accountability adopted Committee Report No. 093-2020 which recommended, among others, the preventive suspension of SB Secretary, Mr. Densing to help him comply with his lacking requirements. On 5 October 2020, Municipal Mayor, Rommel C. Arnado previously filed before the Civil Service Commission (CSC) Regional Office No. 10 a case against SB Secretary Densing for Gross Neglect of Duty, Grave Misconduct, being Notoriously Undesirable, Gross Insubordination, Discourtesy in the Course of Official Duties and Unprofessionalism. Meanwhile, it is also represented in the subject letter that Municipal Mayor Arnado in his burning desire to go after those who dared oppose him and through sheer vindictiveness filed a case before the Office of the Ombudsman — Mindanao for Estafa through Abuse of Confidence against

Furthermore, the Department is proscribed by its internal rules as provided in DILG Memorandum Order No. 2010-021 to act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: xxx 1. Those containing facts that are justifiable in nature. Justiciable issues are those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy; 2. Those presumptively valid acts; e.g., enacted ordinance, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; 3. Those that are litis pendencia or pending litigation, except when the court itself, requests for opinion. In the event that the opinion has been rendered by the Department and its field officers without knowledge or the information that a case involving the issues raised in the query is pending in court, such opinion shall automatically be deemed ineffective ; and 4. Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government." Be that as it may, the following provisions of law/principles are discussed to guide you and the either parties in your next course/s of action. On the first issue, the Department opined in DILG Legal Opinion No. 05, series of 2020, citing DILG Legal Opinion No. 032-94, dated 02 March 1994, that: "Relevantly, under Section 445 (a) of RA 7160, the municipal vice-mayor shall 'appoint all officials and employees of the sangguniang bayan, except those whose manner of appointment is specifically provided in this Code." Considering that sanggunian employees are appointees of the vice-mayor, they are, therefore, within the latter's administrative authority, as all their duties and functions relate to services to be rendered in the sanggunian. It being so, the imposition of disciplinary actions/measures against officials and employees of the sanggunian are within the jurisdiction of the vice-mayor." I Supplemental to Memorandum Order No. 2010-01 dated 4 March 2010 (Request for Legal Opinion from the DILG Central Office)

you and your daughter Michelle Jubas Buhia. Apparently, the matter has been referred to the SB Committee on Laws which expeditiously recommended to the Office of Municipal Mayor Arnado on what penalty/grounds/ruling the latter can do for what disciplinary actions especially that the accused was an elected official. It would not be amiss to note that ostensibly, seven (7) out of the ten (10) members of the Sangguniang Bayan are staunched ally of the Municipal Mayor, while the three (3) remaining members composed the minority, as such Municipal Mayor Amado has the majority of the SB members supporting his every proposal even if such is no longer within the bounds of the law. Hence, your request for this Department's opinion on the following queries, which we quoted in toto: I. Does the Sangguniang Bayan through the SB Committee on Laws have the jurisdiction and/or authority to hear, investigate and recommend the suspension of an appointive municipal official such as the Secretary to the Sangguniang Bayan in-this-partieuIaF 2. Does the Sangguniang Bayan through the SB Committee on Laws have the jurisdiction and/or authority to investigate, inquire and/or recommend to the Municipal Mayor for the imposition of penalty/grounds/ruling for disciplinary actions against an elective municipal official such as the Municipal Vice-Mayor and Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Bayan in this particular case?; and 3. [Whether or not] the Municipal Mayor is clothed with authority to enforce any penalty/grounds/ruling for disciplinary actions against an elective municipal official such as the Municipal Vice- Mayor and Presiding Officer of the Sangguniang Bayan in this particular case? We regret to inform you that we cannot render an opinion on the above- enumerated issues due to the pendency of issues with the Civil Service Commission vis-å-vis SB Secretary Densing and with the Office of the Ombudsman vis-a-vis your concerns. We might pre-empt the resolution of the issues by the aforestated bodies.

As to the second and third issues, Section 61 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Govemment Code of 1991 enumerates the disciplining authority vis-a-vis erring elective official of the municipality such as the Vice- Mayor, thus: Section 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints.—A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and xxxx This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly.Thank you. BY Very truly yours, ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN, CESO Ill Officer-in-Charge Office of the Undersecretary for Local Government LLLS/27/17 Copy fumished: DIRECTOR ARNEL M.
